entries.description: A malformed resource identifier reaches the database unvalidated and surfaces as an unhandled HTTP 500.
entries.currentState: NEW AT §297A, FOUND BY A SINGLE AUTHORISED PROBE AND CONFIRMED IN PRODUCTION. One authenticated GET /files/<malformed> returned HTTP 500 in 313 ms. The production log names the cause exactly: QueryFailedError: invalid input syntax for type uuid. The route takes the path parameter straight to a TypeORM lookup with no shape validation, so Postgres rejects it and the resulting driver error is unhandled. WHAT WAS CHECKED BEFORE CLASSIFYING IT. The response body returned to the client is the generic {"statusCode":500,"message":"Internal server error"} — NO stack trace, NO SQL, and the supplied value is NOT echoed back. The route is behind JwtGuard, so it is not reachable unauthenticated. The probe referenced no real resource and crossed no tenant boundary. Nothing was mutated. So this is NOT an authorization bypass, NOT cross-tenant exposure, NOT sensitive-data disclosure, NOT a destructive mutation, and NOT a critical availability risk — none of the §297A mandatory-escalation categories applies, and §297A therefore registered it rather than stopping. TWO SECONDARY OBSERVATIONS. The attacker-supplied value IS echoed into the server-side log line, which is operator-side and is the caller's own input rather than customer data, but it is a user-controlled value reaching the log store. And an authenticated caller can produce cheap 500s at will, which is the one thing that makes this more than cosmetic: five of them inside five minutes would raise a real service.error_rate_exceeded and reach the operator, so this defect is also a route to manufacturing alert noise. §297B REPRODUCED IT FIVE MORE TIMES TO EXERCISE THE MONITORING THRESHOLD, AND THAT DOES NOT MAKE IT ACCEPTABLE BEHAVIOUR. Six genuine unhandled 500s have now been observed on this path in production. The defect is unchanged, its severity is unchanged, and it was deliberately NOT repaired while it was being used as an instrument — repairing the stimulus while validating the layer downstream of it would have destroyed the only confirmed qualifying condition the product has. It must not be read as normal endpoint behaviour, and the monitoring closure does not depend on it remaining broken: any qualifying error-severity condition reaches the same path.
entries.evidence: Production probe 2026-09-14T23:43:56Z, HTTP 500, 313 ms. Render log store, same second: "QueryFailedError: invalid input syntax for type uuid". Generic client body confirmed from the response bytes.
entries.remediation: Validate the identifier shape before it reaches the query — a UUID pipe on the route parameter, returning 400 — or catch the driver error and return 404 so a malformed identifier is indistinguishable from an absent one. The second is the better default on a route that reads by id, because it also avoids confirming which identifiers are well-formed. Audit sibling routes that take an id path parameter: this route was probed, the others were not, and the same pattern is likely.
entries.retestRequirement: GET /files/<malformed> returns a contained 4xx and raises no operational event; a valid-but-absent id still returns 404.
entries.note: Deliberately NOT repaired in §297A. The section authorised using an existing fault as monitoring evidence and repairing it only if it prevented safe completion or created a critical exposure; neither applies. It is also NOT a Threshold-B blocker: it needs an authenticated account, discloses nothing, and changes no state, so it does not stand between the product owner and their own internal use. §297B: classification preserved unchanged. The alert payload it produced carries path "/files/:id" and failureKind "QueryFailedError" and does NOT contain the malformed identifier, so using it as an instrument disclosed nothing.

entries.description: The employer-pro promo code is inert: registration reports planCode "pro" and promoApplied true, and the very next login resolves the account to free with fullSafeScope false.
entries.currentState: FOUND AT §300 WHILE ATTEMPTING THE HZ-9 PROOF, AND MEASURED END TO END IN PRODUCTION. POST /auth/register with a configured promo returned 201, planCode "pro", promoApplied true; the JWT minted at the next login carried planCode "free", effectivePlanCode "free", subscriptionStatus "none", billingEntitlements.fullSafeScope false; POST /hazlenz/classify returned 402 PAID_SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED. ROOT CAUSE, TWO FAULTS COMPOUNDING: (1) AuthService.resolveSessionContext calls getBillingStatus({userId, email, planCode, type}) and does NOT pass user.subscriptionStatus, although the promo registration deliberately writes subscriptionStatus "active" onto the user row next to planCode "pro"; (2) in getBillingStatus, `normalizeStripeSubscriptionStatus(...) || (fallbackTier === "free" ? "none" : "active")` has an UNREACHABLE right-hand branch, because normalizeStripeSubscriptionStatus ends in `return "none"` and never returns a falsy value. The branch exists precisely to treat a paid tier carrying no explicit status as active. So fallbackStatus is always "none", resolveAccessTier("pro","none",null) returns "free", and effectivePlanCode — which prefers billingSnapshot.tier — discards the user row's "pro". NO CUSTOMER IS AFFECTED TODAY: EMPLOYER_PRO_PROMO_CODES was empty in production before §300 and is empty again after it, so no promo account has ever existed in production. The defect is latent, not live.
entries.evidence: verification/current/hz9-entitlement-blocker-300/SECTION-300-PHASE1-HZ9-BLOCKER.json. Source: src/auth/auth.service.ts (register, resolveSessionContext); src/billing/billing.service.ts (getBillingStatus); src/billing/subscription-status.ts (normalizeStripeSubscriptionStatus, resolveAccessTier).
entries.remediation: Pass the user's own subscriptionStatus into getBillingStatus, and repair the dead fallback so a paid tier with no explicit status resolves as intended rather than through a branch that can never run. Add a test that a promo-registered account reaches fullSafeScope, because the absence of one is why a success response could advertise a plan the account does not have.
entries.retestRequirement: A promo-registered account logs in with planCode pro and receives 200 from POST /hazlenz/classify.
entries.note: Registered at §300, NOT repaired: §300 Phase 2 is gated on Phase 1 passing and this is neither HZ-6 nor HZ-7. It is also the reason HZ-9 could not be proven — it was the only route to fullSafeScope that does not modify the production database directly.

entries.currentState: MECHANISM IMPLEMENTED AND PROVEN; NO DESTINATION CONFIGURED IN PRODUCTION. §291 built the push half MO-1 asks for: every error-severity operational event is dispatched to a configured destination, repeated 5xx raise ONE service.error_rate_exceeded rather than one alert per request, and one alert per event kind per 15-minute window keeps an outage from becoming a mail storm. Proven against a real induced storage failure: six consecutive 500s produced THREE alerts — one per event kind plus one rate alert — while 401, 404 and 400 produced none, which is the noise policy §291 specified. §291 did NOT invent a production destination, because choosing an alerting channel has a cost and an account attached. /health/ready now reports alerting: NOT_CONFIGURED, so "nothing is watching" is a visible fact rather than a silent assumption. THIS IS NOT YET MONITORING IN PRODUCTION. §292 SEARCHED FOR AN EXISTING DESTINATION AND FOUND NONE. Project documentation names exactly one established operational destination — the Render service notification (notifyOnFail, email to the workspace owner) — and that is a PLATFORM channel for deploy and service failure that the application cannot publish into. There is no Slack, PagerDuty, Sentry or webhook configuration anywhere in the repository or either platform; Render has zero webhooks and no log stream; and the Resend credential that would enable the email channel does not exist (EM-2). §292 did NOT invent a destination. The noise policy was re-proven on the §292 build against a real receiver: 401, 404, 400, duplicate-register and 402 produced ZERO alerts, while one qualifying 500 produced two alerts — one per event kind — delivered in 4 ms with metadata carrying no content. §293 RE-VERIFIED THE ABSENCE INDEPENDENTLY AND FOUND THE REMEDIATION INSTRUCTION UNDERSTATED. The 41 production environment variables were read again: OPERATIONAL_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL, OPERATIONAL_ALERT_EMAIL and RESEND_API_KEY are all still absent, Render still has zero webhooks and slackEnabled false, Vercel still has zero marketplace integrations and zero storage stores, and no Resend credential exists anywhere in the repository or in standard client configuration locations. /health/ready still reports alerting: NOT_CONFIGURED. §293 additionally read the dispatch path and found that the email channel needs a THIRD variable the remediation did not name — see MO-2 — so the remediation text below is corrected rather than repeated. §294 REPAIRED THE CHANNEL BUT COULD NOT CONFIGURE IT. The false-green path MO-2 described no longer exists: setting the two variables the register used to name now leaves /health/ready reporting NOT_CONFIGURED with the missing sender named, rather than reporting a configured channel that delivers nothing. MO-1 itself is untouched by that, because no destination, credential or sender was supplied and none was invented. Production configuration is unchanged. §295 DEPLOYED THE HARDENED BUILD AND FOUND THAT THE OWNER BOUNDARY IS LARGER THAN §293 STATED. The §294 candidate is live on both halves at 87491ed9 and /health/ready serves the three-state contract, still reporting NOT_CONFIGURED. The remaining work was recorded as "name a destination and supply a credential", and for the EMAIL architecture the owner selected that is incomplete: Resend sends only from a domain VERIFIED IN THE ACCOUNT, verification is DNS records on a domain the owner CONTROLS, and the Vercel account holds ZERO custom domains — the product is served from safety-insite.vercel.app, whose apex vercel.app belongs to Vercel and cannot be verified by this owner. No Resend session exists in the owner's browser either, so no account is evidenced. The email path therefore needs a domain BEFORE it needs a credential. The WEBHOOK path needs none of that, and §293's instruction not to prefer a webhook "merely to obtain a faster green gate if an approved Resend configuration is now available" does not bite, because one is not available. The choice between them is now a genuine product decision rather than a shortcut, and it is recorded in the §295 runbook. §296 SELECTED THE ARCHITECTURE AND PROVED THE BRANCH, AND STILL COULD NOT CLOSE. The product owner chose the WEBHOOK architecture — deliberately, and not on cost or speed: the product name is to be replaced before external beta, and a verified sending domain is exactly the infrastructure that entrenches a name, whereas a webhook URL is one environment variable to replace. §296 then found that the webhook branch had never been executed since §294 rewrote the dispatcher: §291 and §292 proved it against a local receiver BEFORE the rewrite, and §294's gate proved the new outcome machinery entirely on the EMAIL branch — the string "webhook" does not appear in it. Closing MO-1 on an unexercised code path would have been closing it on the same kind of assumption MO-2 was, so the branch was proven first: npm run test:296-webhook-channel, 15/15, 0 network, 0 provider calls. WHAT REMAINS IS A DESTINATION, AND IT IS STILL AN OWNER ACTION. §296 searched the already-authorised surface for a monitored receiver and found none: there is no Slack session and no workspace (the sign-in page asks for a workspace URL), no Discord session, and none of GitHub, Render, Vercel, Neon or Stripe offers an inbound receiver that accepts an unauthenticated POST and surfaces it where a human looks. Inventing a URL, standing up an ephemeral receiver, or pointing the channel at something nobody reads were all forbidden and would each have produced a green gate over nothing watching — which is precisely the failure MO-2 was. §297A CONFIGURED THE DESTINATION, PROVED THE RECEIVER, AND STILL COULD NOT CLOSE — FOR A REASON THAT IS THE PRODUCT WORKING. The webhook destination is configured in production and /health/ready now reports alerting CONFIGURED, channel webhook, lastDelivery null. The receiver was proven reachable out of band: one hand-sent message, clearly labelled as NOT a product alert, was accepted by the destination, retrieved independently through a subscriber poll, and confirmed RENDERED IN THE OWNER'S SUBSCRIBED CLIENT. Then one authorised probe produced a GENUINE unhandled production 500 (SE-5). AND IT CORRECTLY RAISED NO ALERT. The §291 noise policy encodes that a single 500 is a bug report and a burst is an outage: service.error_rate_exceeded fires only when 5 server errors occur inside 5 minutes. After the probe, production reported serverErrorsInWindow 1 against a threshold of 5, lastDelivery null, and the destination still held only the out-of-band message. So the live chain cannot be completed by a single 500 — not because anything is broken, but because the aggregation policy is doing exactly what it was built to do. §297A forbade repeating the probe, forbade lowering the threshold to make the test easier, and forbade falling back to breaking storage without a new decision. All three were respected. WHAT IS NOW KNOWN THAT WAS NOT: every link in the chain is independently proven except the trigger. Configuration truthfulness, destination reachability, subscriber receipt and human visibility are all evidenced live; the webhook branch's dispatch and outcome recording were proven at §296; and the quiet path is proven live, because a real 500 plus a 404 plus a 401 produced zero alerts on a CONFIGURED channel. What remains is a qualifying condition, and choosing how to produce one is a product-owner decision. CLOSED AT §297B ON ACTUAL MONITORED RECEIPT. The §297A error had aged out — production reported serverErrorsInWindow 0 after 15.5 minutes against a 5-minute window — so it was NOT counted, and a fresh sequence of exactly five requests was run against the same confirmed SE-5 path. The progression is the policy stating itself: requests 1 through 4 returned 500 with serverErrorsInWindow climbing 1, 2, 3, 4 and lastDelivery NULL at every step — four genuine production errors and not one alert. The fifth crossed the threshold and produced exactly ONE service.error_rate_exceeded, dispatched to the webhook and accepted with HTTP 200 at 2026-09-14T23:59:49.031Z, 272 ms after the monitoring event. FIVE ERRORS PRODUCED ONE ALERT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THE AGGREGATION. The alert ARRIVED: retrieved independently through a subscriber poll as message pzDPWfb8CuTV, and confirmed RENDERED IN THE PRODUCT OWNER'S SUBSCRIBED CLIENT. Afterwards /health/ready still reports alerting CONFIGURED, channel webhook, and lastDelivery DELIVERY_ACCEPTED status 200 — the configuration remained truthful through the dispatch rather than only before it. THE TRANSMITTED PAYLOAD WAS RECONFIRMED ON THE ACTUAL BYTES, not on a local reproduction: 311 bytes carrying source, event, severity, at, environment, release and five metadata fields — path "/files/:id", method, statusCode, countInWindow and failureKind "QueryFailedError". The malformed identifier that CAUSED the errors does not appear anywhere in it, because path is the ROUTE PATTERN and failureKind is the error CLASS NAME rather than its message. That is the §268 redaction working on live production data.

entries.description: The email alert channel reports itself configured without a deliverable sender, and the delivery result is discarded, so a rejected alert is indistinguishable from a delivered one.
entries.currentState: NEW AT §293, FOUND BY READING THE DISPATCH PATH RATHER THAN BY RUNNING IT. Three limbs, all in backend/src/observability/operational-alerts.ts. (1) describeAlertConfiguration() returns configured: true, channel: email on OPERATIONAL_ALERT_EMAIL and RESEND_API_KEY alone, but dispatchOperationalAlert() sends from: PASSWORD_RESET_FROM_EMAIL || 'alerts@safety-insite.invalid'. The .invalid TLD is reserved by RFC 2606 and can never be a verified Resend sending domain, so with only those two variables set every send is rejected while /health/ready reports the channel as configured. That inverts the §291 guarantee that made MO-1 defensible — "nothing is watching" being a VISIBLE fact rather than a silent assumption — because alerting: configured would then mean nothing is watching. (2) Both the webhook and email branches are void fetch(...).catch(() => undefined) with no logging of a non-2xx response. Not throwing is correct and is the same rule §287 applied to the audit write; not RECORDING is not, and it means an unverified domain, a revoked key or a suspended account produces no signal inside the product. (3) The §291 and §292 alert proofs both ran against a local HTTP webhook receiver. No committed harness exercises the email branch at all, so the channel the owner selected at §293 has zero executed coverage. CLOSED AT §294 ON EXECUTABLE PROOF, BEFORE ANY CREDENTIAL EXISTS — which is the only order in which this defect could be closed honestly, because a configured channel would have hidden it. Three structural repairs. (1) resolveEmailChannel() is now the ONE place that decides what the email channel requires, and describeAlertConfiguration() and dispatchOperationalAlert() are both written in terms of it, so they cannot state different requirements — the parity is structural rather than a convention a later edit is trusted to keep. (2) There is NO fallback sender. alerts@safety-insite.invalid is gone and nothing replaced it: an absent or structurally undeliverable sender leaves the channel NOT_CONFIGURED with the sender named as the reason. Undeliverability is tested by reserved TLD (RFC 2606 .invalid/.example/.test and RFC 6761 .localhost/.local) rather than by naming one retired string, so the next such address is caught too, and the same rule is applied to the RECIPIENT. (3) Dispatch is still launched and abandoned with respect to the customer request — never awaited, and it still cannot turn a succeeded operation into a 500 — but the promise now resolves into evidence rather than into undefined: every attempt produces exactly one of DELIVERY_ACCEPTED, PROVIDER_REJECTED, NETWORK_FAILURE or MALFORMED_RESPONSE, emitted as monitoring.alert_delivered (info) or monitoring.alert_delivery_failed (warning). Both are deliberately below error severity so the dispatcher cannot alert about its own failure through the channel that just failed. /health/ready gained a third state, DEGRADED, for a configured channel whose last attempt did not succeed; service readiness is unaffected in all three states, because a mail provider having a bad ten minutes must not stop Safety InSite serving inspections. SENDER SEMANTICS — option A, shared, with an optional override: monitoring uses PASSWORD_RESET_FROM_EMAIL by default so one verified domain serves both monitoring and EM-2, and OPERATIONAL_ALERT_FROM_EMAIL overrides it if operations mail should ever be distinguishable. No new REQUIRED configuration was introduced and the owner still supplies three values. §296 EXTENDED THE PROOF TO THE OTHER BRANCH. §294 proved the outcome machinery entirely on the email channel; §296 proved it on the webhook channel — all four bounded outcomes, DEGRADED and recovery, dedupe and ceiling, containment, the quiet statuses through the real ServerErrorAlertFilter, and the measured wire payload. It also recorded one deliberate asymmetry: the webhook branch does NOT apply the email branch's MALFORMED_RESPONSE rule, because an arbitrary receiver has no acknowledgement schema, so 2xx IS the acknowledgement. Discord answers 204 and Slack answers 200 with the body "ok"; a dispatcher that required a JSON acknowledgement would have reported every successful Slack delivery as a failure.

entries.description: The deterministic evidence extractor asserts employeeExposure=false from a bare "nobody" or "no one" anywhere in the observation, which CONTRADICTS the exposure predicate and suppresses the applicable standard.
entries.currentState: NEW AT §298, FOUND IN PRODUCTION ON A REAL ANALYSIS AND CAUGHT BY EXPERT HAZLENZ ITSELF. THE MECHANISM, read from the shipped source and reproduced by executing the shipped expression: backend/src/hazlenz/evidence/shared-evidence-facts.ts line 473 builds `noExposure` as an alternation whose last two members are the BARE words `nobody` and `no one`, anchored to nothing about exposure, and line 478 then writes employeeExposure=false at confidence 0.98 with status 'confirmed'. WHAT IT DID TO A REAL OBSERVATION: the §298 walkthrough note contains "Nobody working up there had a harness on" and "Nobody was injured" — two sentences that describe a fall hazard, one of which PRESUPPOSES people working at height. Either matches on its own; removing both removes the match; the intended sense ("no employees were exposed") still matches through the anchored alternative. CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED: 29 CFR 1910.28 came back status CONTRADICTED at confidence 0.05, "Suppressed because submitted evidence contradicts: employee access or exposure", with the other two required predicates SUPPORTED; assessmentDisposition read 'controlled_condition'; the executive summary read "Top uncertainty: Employee exposure is not clearly described"; and the generated customer report printed "HazLenz basis: Candidate only; missing: employee access or exposure" directly beneath the paragraph that describes the exposure. BLAST RADIUS: `e.noExposure` gates 'worker in fall zone', 'occupational employee exposure' (x2) and 'miner exposure during the work shift' (x2) in evidence-foundation.ts, so it reaches OSHA general industry, OSHA construction and MSHA rules. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the hazard was NOT missed. The deterministic decomposition still raised fall-protection at riskBand Critical with imminentDanger true and requiresShutdown true. The engine produced internally inconsistent output on one observation — the hazard escalated and its regulatory basis suppressed — and it is the regulatory half that is degraded. §299: CLOSED BY SEMANTIC-FAMILY REPAIR. ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED AT THE SOURCE: a negative person quantifier ("nobody", "no one", "no <person-noun>") is not an assertion about exposure — what it negates is decided by THE PREDICATE IT SCOPES OVER, and the pre-§299 expression treated every generic negation word as interchangeable. REPAIR: backend/src/hazlenz/evidence/person-negation-semantics.ts classifies each quantified clause into one of four predicate senses — PRESENCE_OR_EXPOSURE, CONTROL_USE, OUTCOME, UNRESOLVED — and ONLY PRESENCE_OR_EXPOSURE reaches employeeExposure. The restrictive modifier is skipped before the predicate is read ("Nobody [working up there] [had a harness on]"), which is the precise mechanism of the defect, and within the predicate the EARLIEST family marker wins so "nobody was on the platform wearing a harness" is still a presence denial. NOTHING ASSERTS THE CONVERSE: the repair REMOVES a false claim and does not invent employeeExposure=true, because the §298 sentence is vacuously true if nobody is up there and deterministic code must not author a safety semantic it cannot establish. NO PHRASE-SPECIFIC EXCEPTION: the §298 sentence appears in no matching rule. MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER on the exact §298 observation, both re-measured locally rather than quoted — BEFORE (at d78150ed, in a read-only worktree): employeeExposure=false confidence 0.98, 29 CFR 1910.28 CONTRADICTED at confidence 0.05, "Suppressed because submitted evidence contradicts: employee access or exposure", assessmentDisposition controlled_condition. AFTER: no employeeExposure fact asserted, 29 CFR 1910.28 UNKNOWN at confidence 0.45, missingPredicates ['employee access or exposure'], "Candidate only; missing: employee access or exposure", assessmentDisposition insufficient_evidence. The standard is a candidate with an open predicate instead of a suppressed one; no CFR citation is manufactured. NO OVERCORRECTION: the same note with "No employees were on the mezzanine" substituted for the harness sentence and every other sentence left in place STILL yields employeeExposure=false at 0.98 and STILL suppresses 1910.28 as CONTRADICTED at 0.05 — the repair narrowed WHICH sentences negate exposure, not WHETHER any do. REGRESSION FAMILY: 27 cases over the ten §299-named groups, 10 of which must still negate and 17 of which must not; the pre-§299 expression is wrong on 16 of the 27 and right on 11, so the family measures a DISTINCTION rather than a direction. It was wrong in BOTH directions — it also missed "Not a single employee was exposed", "No employees on the elevated surface" and "None of the crew were on the roof", so genuine no-exposure handling is improved as well as narrowed. EXPERT DISAGREEMENT UNAFFECTED: all four disagreement types and all three targets intact, no file under any Expert path added or modified (checked against d78150ed over tracked changes AND untracked additions), and the deterministic projection Expert receives still carries a named open predicate for Expert to contest. PRODUCTION STATUS (§299): the repaired code IS what production is running — /health/version reports gitCommit 317daba8 with versionSourceStatus RENDER_GIT_COMMIT, corroborated by Render deploy dep-daka1lh42hec739qlfo0 (requestedCommit 317daba8, status live), and the Render build command is bare tsc over backend/src so the deployed dist is compiled from exactly that source. THAT IS ARTIFACT-IDENTITY EVIDENCE, NOT A LIVE BEHAVIOURAL EXECUTION, and it is recorded as such rather than as a live verification. The live behavioural half is NOT_EXERCISED: POST /hazlenz/classify is guarded by JwtGuard + EntitlementGuard(fullSafeScope) + RolesGuard, so exercising it in production would require creating a synthetic production account and granting an entitlement — production writes §299 did not authorise. Two non-invasive routes were attempted and both need an owner action (an SSH key registered with Render for an in-container read-only probe; a production database credential to reset the §298 synthetic account the way §298 did). THE LOCAL HALF IS COMPLETE AND EXECUTED: 117 assertions through the shipped buildEvidenceFacts() and applyEvidenceFoundation(). §300: THE LIVE HALF IS NOW DISCHARGED. The repaired interpretation was exercised behaviourally through the deployed production runtime (see HZ-9), so HZ-4 no longer rests on artifact identity. SEPARATELY, that live proof revealed HZ-10: a SECOND, INDEPENDENT COPY of the same bare-negation error in backend/src/hazlenz/display/hazlenz-evidence-boundary.ts, downstream of everything §299 repaired and exercised. entries.description: A finding finalized from a review that cites an Expert analysis carries no risk snapshot, so it reaches the customer report with no severity and no applicable standard.
entries.currentState: NEW AT §298, MEASURED END TO END IN PRODUCTION. Risk is computed at deterministic reconciliation time, and no finding is reconciled from any Expert analysis by design — so a finding created by finalizing an Expert-cited review has riskSnapshot NULL. The §298 report printed that finding as 'Not rated' with 'APPLICABLE STANDARD: Not established for this specific finding', while the deterministic finding naming the same hazard printed Critical, severity 5, likelihood 4, risk score 20, with a corrective action. THE REPORT IS HONEST ABOUT IT — the executive summary states '1 finding(s) have no established risk rating' and directs a qualified person to rate it before closure, and nothing fabricates a severity — so this is a capability gap, not a false claim.
entries.remediation: A product decision before an engineering one: either Expert-derived findings get a risk derivation of their own, or the workflow does not offer finalization from an Expert-cited review as a way of creating a NEW finding, or the reviewer is required to supply the risk (FinalizeFindingDto already accepts riskAssessment). Do not have deterministic code infer a severity from Expert's posture — that would be deterministic code authoring safety semantics.
entries.retestRequirement: Whichever option is chosen, a finalized Expert-derived finding reaches the report either with a severity whose provenance is stated, or with the absence stated as it is now and no path that silently produces an unrated finalized finding.
entries.note: §298 exercised BOTH the Expert-cited and the deterministic finalization paths on one observation, so the report carries two findings for one hazard. The duplication is an artefact of the test; the missing severity is not.

Every §299 local proof still passes: §299 exercised buildEvidenceFacts and applyEvidenceFoundation, and this module sits downstream of both, so neither the local suite nor the artifact-identity argument could have reached it. MECHANISM: in enforceHazLenzEvidenceBoundary(), `affirmativelyNoExposure` is a regular expression whose alternation includes the BARE words `nobody` and `no one`, anchored to nothing about exposure — the identical shape §299 repaired elsewhere. It ALONE sets `affirmativelyControlled`, which sets assessmentDisposition=controlled_condition, sets mustDemote=true (emptying primaryCitation, primaryStandards, suggestedStandards and standards) and OVERWRITES result.risk with riskScore 0, riskBand Controlled, imminentDanger false, requiresShutdown false, plus a LOW-priority "Verify the controlled condition" action. A SECOND ALTERNATION in the same function (nobody | no one | passed | within | fully | complete | closed | secured, gated behind controlsPresent>0 and controlsMissing===0) is the same class of error and did not fire here only because no structuredObservation was supplied; it must be examined in the same repair.
